a: O(1) means constant time regardless of input size.
O(n) means time grows linearly with input size.
O(n log n) is typical of efficient comparison sorts like mergesort.
O(n^2) often appears in nested loops over the same data.
Binary search finds a target in a sorted array in O(log n) time.
Average lookup in a hash map is O(1); worst case can be O(n).
Stack is LIFO: last in, first out.
Queue is FIFO: first in, first out.
BFS explores level by level; DFS goes deep along one path first.
DP solves overlapping subproblems by storing results of smaller problems.
